structured_output.summary: The head files single with CA AGI of about $22,535: wages of $17,443, less the $2,778 401(k) deferral, plus the $8,000 403(b) distribution, less the $130 IRA deduction. Medical costs fall below the 7.5% floor, so the standard deduction applies. Using the last amounts published before the 2026-07-03 freeze (the 2025 FTB figures: $5,706 standard deduction, $153 exemption credit, 1% bracket up to $11,079), tax is $225.79. Subtracting the $153 exemption credit and the $60 renter's credit (§17053.5(k)(2) falls back to $60 because the $250 enhancement was not funded) leaves $12.79. The engine followed exactly this path and got $12.78. The $0 consensus depends on the 2026 indexed amounts, which were not published until after the freeze, or on errors such as a nonexistent disability exemption credit or treating CalEITC as nonrefundable.
structured_output.stage1_error: Stage 1 used the 2026 indexed parameters (3.4% CCPI, giving a $5,900 standard deduction, a $158 exemption credit and a $11,456 top for the 1% bracket). By its own account these were published after the 2026-07-03 reference-law freeze. Under the benchmark's frozen-law convention, the amounts governing tax year 2026 are the last ones the agency published before the freeze, the 2025 FTB figures ($5,706 / $153 / $11,079). Stage 1 itself showed that those figures reproduce the reference ($12.79). Its conclusion that the law supports the $0 consensus therefore rests on post-freeze amounts and should not stand. Its other findings were correct: no disability exemption credit under R&TC 17054, a $60 renter's credit under the 17053.5(k)(2) fallback, no medical itemization, and the disability exception to the early-distribution tax.
